title: The footer indents 44px past a manifest toggle nothing renders
body:
## Summary
`.ln-foot` pads its content 44px in from the sheet's start edge to clear "the kit's manifest toggle", and no source in the repo renders that toggle, so the breadcrumb and legend sit 44px right of the masthead and stage edge they should align with.

## Description
`examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/style/chrome/foot.css:10` sets `padding-inline-start: 44px` under a comment saying the kit's `position: fixed` manifest toggle sits bottom-left. The kit's `.dk-manifest*` rules were removed by 7d3cf3d because nothing had ever drawn them (`git grep dk-manifest -- examples apps packages` is empty), and the bridge (`packages/athena-bridge`) injects no DOM. The masthead and the stage start at the root's padding (`base/the-sheet.css:41`, `--ln-s5`), so the footer row is misaligned by 44px at every width, including the 42rem step where the root padding drops to 12px and 44px is 11% of a 390px phone. The one thing that does sit bottom-left is Next's dev-mode indicator (`next.config.ts` sets no `devIndicators`), which ships only under `next dev` - so removing the indent makes the crumb collide with that bubble in dev while fixing production. Fixed means a decision: align the footer and move the dev indicator (`devIndicators: { position: "bottom-right" }`, an app-shell file), or keep the gutter and say it is for the dev indicator.

## Flow
- open the Lanes at any level; the footer's crumb starts 44px right of the masthead's left edge
- at <= 42rem the root padding is 12px and the footer still adds 44px
- the toggle the comment names is not in the DOM (no source renders `.dk-manifest-toggle`)

## Expected impact
Anyone reading the sheet top to bottom sees the footer's left edge out of line with everything above it; on a phone the breadcrumb loses 44px of a 390px row. Measured by the footer's start offset against the masthead's (44px today, 0 after). Could break: in `next dev` the dev indicator would overlap the first crumb unless it is moved.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the footer aligns with the sheet and a phone gets its 44px back
Before: footer content starts 44px past the root padding at every width; the control it clears does not exist in source
After: predicted 0px offset; the dev indicator needs its own home
Method: simulation - CSS arithmetic and a zero-renderer grep; seeing the collision trade-off needs the running dev window, which this round may not start
Result: better
Gate: direction
evidence:
examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/style/chrome/foot.css:10  padding-inline-start: 44px;
examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/style/chrome/foot.css:3-8  "The kit's manifest toggle is `position: fixed` in the bottom-left corner"
git grep dk-manifest -- examples apps packages  -> (no output); removed by 7d3cf3d "the manifest drawer rules nothing has ever drawn"
examples/ledgerbox/next.config.ts  no devIndicators -> Next's dev indicator sits bottom-left under next dev

title: Hover on the gated and danger buttons swaps the gate's orange frame for grey
body:
## Summary
`.ln-btn:hover:not(:disabled)` scores (0,3,0) and sets `border-color: var(--ln-mute)`, which beats every `.ln-btn[data-kind]` variant at (0,2,0): under the pointer the GATED control loses the one hue the sheet reserves for it.

## Description
`examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/style/level2/l2-the-card-2.css:168` is the hover rule; the variants are `l2-the-card-3.css:1` (`gate`: orange border and text), `:6` (`danger`: orange fill and border) and `l2-the-card-2.css:181` (`primary`: ink fill and border). `base/tokens.css` says of `--ln-gate`: "The one hue reserved for a held gate. Spent on nothing else." At the moment a reader is about to press a gated act (`Gate.tsx:88`) or confirm it (`Gate.tsx:71`), its frame turns the grey of every ordinary button; the primary button's ink edge goes grey too. Fixed means a hover that keeps each variant's own hue (for example a variant-scoped hover, or a hover that changes the ground rather than the border) - a treatment choice, which is why it is carded.

## Flow
- open an invoice's decision list; hover the gated act's button (data-kind="gate")
- specificity (0,3,0) > (0,2,0): border-color becomes --ln-mute while the text stays --ln-gate
- arm it; hover the confirm (data-kind="danger"): orange fill with a grey edge

## Expected impact
Readers of the decision dialog: the AUTO/GATED distinction the surface exists to teach is weakest exactly under the pointer. Measured by the computed border-color of each data-kind button while hovered (--ln-mute today, its own hue after). Could break: the ghost variant's hover border, which is the one variant that wants the grey.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a gated control keeps its gate hue while it is pointed at
Before: 3 of 4 data-kind variants lose their border colour on hover (specificity arithmetic on the four rules)
After: predicted 0 of 4
Method: simulation - specificity read off the rules; the hover treatment to replace it is a visual call this round cannot see without a browser
Result: better
Gate: direction
evidence:
examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/style/level2/l2-the-card-2.css:168  .ln-btn:hover:not(:disabled) { border-color: var(--ln-mute); }   (0,3,0)
examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/style/level2/l2-the-card-3.css:1  .ln-btn[data-kind="gate"] { border-color: var(--ln-gate); ... }   (0,2,0)
examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/style/level2/l2-the-card-3.css:6  .ln-btn[data-kind="danger"] { background: var(--ln-gate); border-color: var(--ln-gate); }
examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/Gate.tsx:71,88  data-kind="danger" / data-kind="gate"

title: Hovering a receding mark lifts its bar but not its amount, glyph or tail
body:
## Summary
The swarm promises that pointing at a receding mark lifts it to full, and only the bar obeys: the mark's printed amount, its glyph and its tail are sibling spans that keep their quiet (0.3) or dim (0.11) opacity while the bar beside them is at 1.

## Description
`examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/style/level0/l0-swarm-2.css:16-41` declares one presence for "the bar, its tail, its amount and its glyph", and `:62-75` says "hover or keyboard focus lifts any mark to full". The bar is lifted twice over - the CSS rule and motion's `whileHover={{ opacity: 1 }}` (`components/lanes/swarm/Lane.tsx:288`, plus `opacity` forced to 1 when hovered or picked at `:213`). The amount (`Lane.tsx:257`), flag (`:269`) and tail (`:248`) are siblings carrying only `data-presence`, so `[data-presence="quiet"]` / `"dim"` keep applying. A labelled quiet mark (labels go to the top balances, `swarm/marks.ts:43`, whether or not they want a decision) therefore shows a full bar under a 30%-opacity amount when pointed at, and a ticked mark the same. Fixed: the wrapper span lifts its three siblings with the bar (e.g. `span:has(> .ln-mark:is(:hover, :focus-visible, [data-open="true"], [data-picked="true"])) > :is(.ln-mark-amount, .ln-mark-flag)` to lit, the tail to 0.42), or the component passes `data-open`/`data-picked` to them.

## Flow
- filter or let a mark go quiet (nothing outstanding) while it is among its lane's labelled balances
- hover it: the bar goes to opacity 1, its amount stays at 0.3, its glyph and tail stay receded
- tick it with select: same split

## Expected impact
Anyone reading the swarm by pointing - the read-out is lifted but the label on the mark itself is not, so the mark reads as half-selected. Measured by the computed opacity of a hovered quiet mark's .ln-mark-amount (0.3 today, 1 after). Could break: the swarm's density if lifted labels overlap neighbours.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a pointed-at mark is lifted whole
Before: 1 of 4 layers (the bar) lifts on hover/focus/pick; 3 stay at the presence opacity
After: predicted 4 of 4
Method: simulation - read off the rules and the markup; the computed opacity needs a rendered page
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/style/level0/l0-swarm-2.css:35  [data-presence="quiet"] { opacity: var(--ln-presence-quiet); }
examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/style/level0/l0-swarm-2.css:70-75  .ln-mark:hover, .ln-mark:focus-visible, .ln-mark[data-open], .ln-mark[data-picked] { opacity: var(--ln-presence-lit); }  - the bar only
examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/swarm/Lane.tsx:248,257,269  <span className="ln-tail"|"ln-mark-amount"|"ln-mark-flag" data-presence={presence}>  siblings, no hover state
examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/swarm/Lane.tsx:288  whileHover={{ opacity: 1 }}  (bar)

title: The toast is set in the system face; the font variables sit on the shell
body:
## Summary `app/layout.tsx` puts the three `next/font` variable classes on `.ln-shell`, and `ToastProvider` renders the toast stack as that div's sibling, so `--font-ln-text` never reaches a toast and every toast falls back to the system UI face. ## Description `examples/ledgerbox/app/layout.tsx:76` - `
{children}
`; `examples/demo-kit/src/ui/Toast.tsx:64` renders `
` after `{children}`, i.e. outside `.ln-shell`. Since e51c4db the toast stack receives the lanes token block, but `--ln-font: var(--font-ln-text), ...` is invalid where `--font-ln-text` is undefined, so `chrome/toast.css`'s `var(--ln-font, ui-sans-serif)` takes its fallback. Every confirmation and refusal toast is the one piece of text on the page not in Space Grotesk. Fixed: `${FONTS}` on `` (or ``), which keeps them on every descendant including the stack. ## Flow - take any act (match, remind, refile); the success or error toast appears bottom-right - its text is in the platform UI face; the sheet beside it is in Space Grotesk / IBM Plex Mono ## Expected impact Everyone who acts on the page sees the only off-brand type on the surface at the moment of feedback. Measured by the toast's computed font-family (system face today, the next/font family after). Could break: nothing visible - the variables are custom properties and only `.ln-*` rules read them. ## Evaluation Claim: user - the toast is set in the sheet's own face Before: 0 of 1 toast stacks inside an element carrying the font variables (layout.tsx:76 vs Toast.tsx:64) After: predicted 1 of 1 with the classes on body Method: simulation - DOM position read off the two sources; the fix is in app/layout.tsx, outside this context's paths Result: better Gate: none
evidence:
examples/ledgerbox/app/layout.tsx:76
{children}
examples/demo-kit/src/ui/Toast.tsx:64
(sibling of children) examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/style/chrome/toast.css font-family: var(--ln-font, ui-sans-serif), system-ui, sans-serif; (fallback taken)
instrument: a source test that the next/font variable classes are on <body> or <html> in app/layout.tsx (an ancestor of the kit's toast stack), red on today's .ln-shell placement

title: The retired token brief and its DTCG file still name edge.css as live
body:
## Summary
`design/pass3-token-brief.md`'s status box and `design/tokens/token.tokens.json`'s `$description` still say the live value authority is `components/edge/edge.css` plus a `/v` index set in `app/globals.css`; both went in 8a8b052.

## Description
c6d05ac corrected the same claim in `design/lb-scales.css` and `design/build-tokens.mjs` (this context's files). The two siblings that make it are outside this context's file list: `examples/ledgerbox/design/pass3-token-brief.md:8-10` ("**The live value authority for the app is `components/edge/edge.css` (direction `edge`) ...; the `/v` index has its own set in `app/globals.css`.**") and `examples/ledgerbox/design/tokens/token.tokens.json:2` ("The live value authority is components/edge/edge.css for the shipped edge direction ..."). `components/edge/` was deleted by 8a8b052, `app/` has no `v/` route, and `README.md:75-77` already says the Strip and `/v` are gone. Fixed: both name `components/lanes/style/base/tokens.css` as the one authority, as the two corrected files now do.

## Flow
- open design/pass3-token-brief.md to learn where a value lives
- follow its bold pointer to components/edge/edge.css: the file does not exist

## Expected impact
Whoever edits ledgerbox's look reads the record's own status box first and is sent to a deleted file. Measured by lines naming a removed path as live (2 today, 0 after). Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the retired records point at the authority that exists
Before: 2 lines (pass3-token-brief.md:8-10, token.tokens.json:2)
After: 0, by the same edit c6d05ac made to the two files in this context
Method: probe - grep for components/edge in examples/ledgerbox/design; the edit is outside this context's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
examples/ledgerbox/design/pass3-token-brief.md:9  `components/edge/edge.css` (direction `edge`) and `components/lanes/style/base/tokens.css`
examples/ledgerbox/design/tokens/token.tokens.json:2  "... The live value authority is components/edge/edge.css for the shipped edge direction ..."
git log --diff-filter=D -- examples/ledgerbox/components/edge/edge.css  -> 8a8b052
examples/ledgerbox/README.md:75-77  "The Strip ... and a direction index at `/v` - is gone, and so is everything under `components/edge/`."
instrument: git grep -n 'components/edge' -- examples/ledgerbox/design: 2 lines before, 0 after

title: Void and draft marks are drawn at 1.6-2.1:1 against their track
body:
## Summary
`--ln-inert` (#35474e) is the swatch for void and draft invoices - their bar on the swarm, their clock mark, their legend swatch, their card's top rule - and it is 1.82:1 on `--ln-surface` and at most 2.08:1 on any ground, under WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 for a graphic needed to read the sheet.

## Description
5ebbe34 gave text in a state colour its own ink (`--tone-ink`, `--ln-faint` for inert), so every WORD about a void or draft invoice now clears 4.5:1. The swatch was left alone on purpose: `base/tokens.css:76-83` argues that a state whose right answer is "nothing" should not compete, and the legend calls inert "not in play". But the mark is still the only thing on the swarm that says the invoice exists (`level0/l0-swarm-2.css:52` paints `.ln-mark` in `--tone` on the `--ln-surface` track), and at 1.82:1 three of the seed's invoices (2 void, 1 draft) are near-invisible bars. Raising the swatch is a judgement about the ramp (how loud "not in play" may be), which is why it is carded rather than built.

## Flow
- L0: find a void or draft invoice in its lane: a #35474e bar on a #0e1a1e track
- L1: its clock mark and the card's top rule in the same value

## Expected impact
Low-vision readers and anyone on a dim screen lose the inert invoices from the swarm entirely. Measured by the swatch's contrast against --ln-surface (1.82:1 today; 3:1 is the floor). Could break: the settled-versus-inert ordering the ramp is built on, if inert ends up louder than good.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every mark on the sheet is perceivable
Before: inert swatch 1.62-2.08:1 on the five grounds (computed from tokens.css)
After: >= 3:1 with a lifted --ln-inert, by the same computation
Method: probe - WCAG relative luminance on the token values; the replacement value is a ramp decision
Result: better
Gate: direction

title: Hovering a lane's name dims it from #fff to #f4fafa, which reads as no feedback
body:
## Summary
The L0 lane head is a button that opens the lane, and its only hover state on the name changes `#fff` to `--ln-ink` (#f4fafa): a 1.07:1 step, slightly DARKER, so pointing at the biggest text on the level visibly does nothing to it.

## Description
`examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/style/level0/l0-swarm.css:250` sets `.ln-lane-name { color: #fff; transition: color ... }` and `:254` `.ln-lane-head:hover .ln-lane-name { color: var(--ln-ink); }`. The transition is declared for a change nobody can see. The lane's spine (`:220`, 0.8 -> 1 on `.ln-lane:hover`) and the track's ground (`level0/l0-swarm-2.css:1`) do respond, so the lane as a whole has feedback; the name - the one text allowed to be big - does not, and the rule that tries goes the wrong way. Fixed: a hover the eye can see on the name (an accent, an underline rule, a weight or opacity change on its siblings) - a treatment choice.

## Flow
- L0: point at a lane's name in the gutter
- the name goes from #ffffff to #f4fafa over --ln-dur-1: no perceptible change

## Expected impact
Mouse readers at L0 get no confirmation that the name is the control that opens the lane. Measured by the luminance step of the hover (1.07:1 today). Could break: the gutter's calm if the chosen hover is loud.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the lane name answers the pointer
Before: hover changes the name by 1.07:1, darker
After: a visible step, per the chosen treatment
Method: simulation - contrast of the two values; what to show instead is a visual call
Result: better
Gate: direction
